section.sectionSummaryBrief: Both aspects of mitzvah observance also apply to the mitzvah of shofar, whose essence transcends measurement and limitation, and through which Jews, rooted in Atzmus, draw down the absolute will.
section.t: Now, these two aspects mentioned above regarding the fulfillment of mitzvos
[because of and in the manner of the command from above,
and the innovation brought about by Yisrael]
are,
as understood,
also present in the mitzvah of shofar blowing.
For although the specific matter of shofar
(from the perspective of the command)
is above measurement and limitation.
For even though the mitzvah of shofar blowing has a measure and limit
(like most mitzvos37)
regarding the number of sounds and the types of sounds38
and the like,
nevertheless its essence
(the content and intention)
of this mitzvah is the service that is above measurement and limitation,
and as is known39
that the matter of shofar blowing is the cry from the depths of the heart that is above the measure and limit of the intellect,
the aspect of "with all your might."
And likewise
(and all the more so)
it is regarding the aspect of the shofar above
(which is brought about by the shofar blowing of man),
that it is above measurement and limitation,
for the shofar above is the aspect of the source of delights that is above a particular delight, as is explained at length in the aforementioned discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek.
Thus,
even though the matter of shofar blowing as it is from the perspective of the command from above is in the aspect of the boundless
[and the command from above is the arousal from above and the empowerment that the service of shofar blowing should be in the manner of "with all your might"],
nevertheless,
since Yisrael are rooted in Atzmus,
they have the ability to make a new will and matter,
the drawing down of the absolute will in His very Essence, which is understood to be above even the aspect of the aforementioned source of delights.
And as mentioned above
(at the beginning of the maamar)
that the matter of "make Me king over you" through shofar blowing is the drawing down
(also)
from the absolute will in His very Essence.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The simple sound of the shofar arouses the simplicity of Yisrael, which is one with the simplicity of Atzmus, and the ultimate perfection of mitzvah observance is to fulfill it with simplicity, thereby becoming one with the simplicity of Atzmus.
section.t: And it can be said that this is also the reason that shofar blowing specifically begins with a simple sound, as is explained at length in the Siddur in the discourse "To understand the matter of shofar blowing according to the intention of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory,"
that this simple sound arouses the simplicity
(and the simplicity)
of Yisrael,
and the simplicity of Yisrael is one with the simplicity of Atzmus40.
And it can be said that this is also one of the reasons for the great effort of the Baal Shem Tov
[and even before his revelation as the Baal Shem Tov]
that simple people, and even young boys and girls, should say "Blessed is G-d" and the like
[and the telling of this detail
(of the conduct of the Baal Shem Tov)
was transmitted to us by our Rebbeim and Nesi'im41,
meaning that this is an instruction and empowerment for each and every one],
for when a simple person says "Blessed is G-d" and the like,
his intention in this is towards Atzmus42
(as is known43
that the fact that the name of Heaven is fluent in the mouth of all is Atzmus).
And likewise it is also in the fulfillment of mitzvos,
that the fulfillment of mitzvos of a simple person is not because through his fulfillment of mitzvos matters are made above,
for a simple person does not know
(yet)
what is above and what is below and what is in the four directions,
but rather because of the command,
"Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us."
And this is the matter of the simple sound of shofar blowing,
that after all the comprehensions of the elevation brought about through the fulfillment of mitzvos,
that through the fulfillment of mitzvos of man, the mitzvos above are made,
and as in the mitzvah of shofar blowing, through this a shofar above is made,
behold, the ultimate perfection is to fulfill the mitzvah with simplicity
[and it can be said that this is in the manner of "their beginning is wedged in their end"44.
For just as the beginning of the service
(before intentions are relevant)
is with simplicity,
so too is it at the conclusion and seal
(perfection)
of the service],
and specifically through this they draw down and become one thing with the simplicity of Atzmus.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The two parables about shofar blowing, seemingly describing negative matters, are actually praises in their inner essence, demonstrating the connection to the King's essential self.
section.t: And based on this, one can also understand what is explained in the discourses of the Rebbe Maharash45
(whose matter is "from the outset, a leap"46)
regarding two parables about shofar blowing.

The first parable, in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, about a king's son who went on a distant road etc., until he even forgot the language of his country and began to cry out with a simple sound
(in the parable there it says the language "with a great voice,"
but in the moral it says the language "with a simple sound"47)
so that his father would recognize him by the innate recognition of the voice.
And the second parable from the great and pious Chassid, the Mahari"tz of Berditchev48, of blessed memory,
about the matter of garments when the king was in the forest
(which are not royal garments at all49),
as is explained there at length regarding the details in this.
For at first glance it is perplexing,
behold it is known that on Rosh Hashanah one must be careful not to mention undesirable matters and attributes,
therefore we do not say confession etc. on Rosh Hashanah50,
and one must speak then only of the virtues and praises of Yisrael,
and here the shofar blowing of Rosh Hashanah is explained with these parables, most of whose details are seemingly matters opposite to praise51
[and for this reason I was precise in the maamar of Erev Rosh Hashanah to mention and speak only the point of the content of these two parables,
and not the details].
And although the aforementioned maamar
(in which these two parables were explained in detail)
was said on Shabbos Parshas Ki Savo and not on Rosh Hashanah52,
nevertheless,
behold these parables are an explanation of the matter of shofar blowing of Rosh Hashanah.
And the great wonder in this,
this itself proves that all the details in these parables are
(in the inwardness of the matters)
for praise53.
